newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Pasminco wants changes at LME.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Pasminco wants changes at LME.

text.p: The world's largest producer of lead and zinc, Pasminco Ltd, on Wednesday called on the London Metal Exchange to make fundamental changes in its operations.

"The amount of money which changes hands between us is dependent on the LME price for our product and we assume that the quoted price is a true and fair reflection of the value of that prodcut at any point in time," David Stewart, managing director of Pasminco told the Australian Metals Conference here.
Producers and consumers of metals are dependent on the LME operating effectively, Stewart said.
"We are entitled to be satisfied that the LME functions in as transparent and efficient manner as possible," Stewart said.
Stewart's comments drew criticism from some of the attendees of the conference, which included the chairman of the LME, Raj Bagri, and its chief executive, David King.
In later remarks, Bagri defended the LME, claiming it was "not somebody's monopoly market."
Bagri said he believed the LME was the most efficeint market for buying, selling and hedging metals and that it was open to suggestions on how it could be improved.
"We are not that complacent or that smug that we think that everything we do is right," Bagri said.
